A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research work, with matching methods, experiments, 19 figures, and Appendices A-C. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and the added NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gibbs, MALA, and HMC experiments measuring convergence, runtime, and sample quality in Section 5, with additional experiments and analyses in Appendices B-C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including measured runtimes, convergence iterations, MMD, effective sample size per second, and sample traces.

M1.justification: The reparameterized samplers, accept-reject relaxation, stochastic and block quasi-DEER variants, coordinate transformation, early stopping, and sliding-window procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 and the explicit block-Jacobian formula move to Appendix A without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: eight-schools Gibbs sampling, German Credit logistic regression, IMDB sentiment embeddings, Rosenbrock sampling, a multimodal Gaussian mixture, and the 501-dimensional item-response model. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments. Figure 6 renames the existing 'naive' quasi-DEER implementation as automatic-differentiation (AD) quasi-DEER; it remains the same comparison. Newly cited Picard-based MCMC work is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the batch and chain-length grids, step sizes, preprocessing, initializations, tolerances, timing procedures, and MMD/ESS evaluation settings. The revisions do not document changed experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both retain the Jacobian-variant comparisons, early-stopping analysis, sliding-window sensitivity, batch/length tradeoffs, multimodal example, and convergence-error and sample-trace analyses. Appendix C redisplays the same evidence without adding or removing an analysis.

E5.justification: The existing seed and repetition counts, timing averages, MMD replications, confidence intervals, and quantile summaries are retained. The new checklist restates existing uncertainty reporting, and Figure 3's simplified axis label leaves the statistical definition in Figure 11 unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the Gibbs summary from both methods converging in dozens of iterations to tens for DEER and 100-150 for quasi-DEER, matching the unchanged Figure 2A. Its runtime summary now focuses on batches of 32 or 64 chains. Plotted results and appendix findings otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Newton residual and updates, cited convergence justification, stochastic diagonal identity, block-matrix derivation, and complexity analysis are retained. v1's Equation 10 reappears as v2's Equation 15 in Appendix A.3. Added theoretical connections introduce no new proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: parallelizing Gibbs, MALA, and HMC across chain length, introducing two efficient quasi-Newton variants, and demonstrating speedups sometimes exceeding an order of magnitude.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly explains diffusion Picard iterations as a quasi-DEER special case using an identity Jacobian. Section 6 adds MCMC contractivity as a potential basis for understanding efficient parallel convergence. Existing limitations concerning multimodality, memory, early stopping, and adaptive HMC remain.

D1.justification: Both versions retain the repository link and implementation settings. The new checklist additionally directs readers to commented supplementary source code for reproducing the main experiments and to its README. These are added reproducibility pointers; the PDFs do not establish a new code release.

R1.justification: v2 identifies Grazzi and Zanella's Picard-based random-walk Metropolis work as closely related and distinguishes its sampler scope and parallelization approach. It also adds connections to parallel Bayesian smoothing, unified sequential-model parallelization, MCMC contractivity, and score-based modeling, modestly broadening and refining the existing positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively condenses and rewrites explanations across the introduction, methods, related work, results, and limitations. It replaces numbered HMC subsubsections with paragraph headings, relocates Algorithm 1 and a formula to Appendix A, and adds a substantial NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format changes typography, margins, figure sizing, captions, and page composition throughout. Retained figures are repacked, including Figures 5-6 and Figures 10-11 sharing pages. Figure 3 simplifies an axis label, and Figure 6 changes 'Naive Q-DEER' to 'AD Q-DEER'; these edits preserve plotted results.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the Gibbs convergence summary to match Figure 2 and more explicitly distinguishes its contribution from closely related Picard-based MCMC research. These improve accuracy and positioning. The condensed presentation makes figures smaller but retains the experimental and algorithmic evidence; the overall gains are limited because the underlying methods and validation are unchanged.
